video_caption: The video opens with a light blue, abstract, fuzzy pattern, which then transitions to display a logo featuring "Ilusys CHEMICAL" with a hexagonal circuit-like graphic on the left, and the title "SYNTHESIS OF SILICIC ACID AND SILICON DIOXIDE." The scene then shifts to a desk laid out with various clear glass containers including a small jar, a measuring cup, a beaker with clear liquid, and a large plastic bottle filled with water. To the right, a white plastic bottle labeled "KYSELINA SOLNÁ" (HYDROCHLORIC ACID) with a cartoon character is visible. The narrator states the objective is to synthesize silicon dioxide and silicic acid using sodium silicate and hydrochloric acid. A white text box appears, listing "CHEMICALS USED: - SODIUM SILICATE - HYDROCHLORIC ACID." This is followed by another white text box providing details about "SODIUM SILICATE" (Na₂SiO₃), also known as waterglass, its uses, and reactions, accompanied by a chemical structure diagram. The narrator mentions that since the concentration is unknown, a small sample will be prepared first. A person's arms then enter the frame, picking up a white syringe and drawing 40ml of liquid, identified by an on-screen text overlay as "SODIUM SILICATE 40ML" and "UNKNOWN CONCENTRATION," from the clear beaker on the right.

A person, wearing a dark long-sleeved shirt and a bracelet on their left wrist, is shown on a table with various clear containers. The person's right hand holds a white syringe, drawing a clear liquid from a glass beaker marked "Metherrand." In the background, a large clear plastic bottle is visible, containing a small amount of liquid at the bottom. To the right of the beaker, a white bottle with a yellow label displaying "RYSELINA SOLNÁ" (Hydrochloric Acid) and "Labar" is present. On the top left, a text overlay reads "SODIUM SILICATE 40ML UNKNOWN CONCENTRATION." The person then lifts the syringe out of the beaker, holding it over the plastic bottle.

A person wearing a dark shirt and a silver bracelet on their left wrist is performing a chemical experiment on a dark countertop. On the table are various containers: a tall clear plastic bottle filled with clear liquid, a clear glass beaker also with clear liquid, a white plastic bottle labeled "KYSELINA SOLNA LABAR" (Hydrochloric acid LABAR), and a small clear bottle. The person uses a syringe to extract liquid from the small clear bottle and adds it in small portions to a clear glass bowl. Immediately after the addition, a white, opaque, gel-like substance forms in the bowl. A text overlay then appears with the "ILUSYS CHEMICAL" logo and information about "SILICIC ACID": "REACTION(THIS VIDEO): NA₂SiO₃ + HCL -> NACL + [SIO.(OH)₂]n. [SIO.(OH)₂]n. IS GENERAL FORMULA FOR FAMILY OF SILICIC ACIDS. FORMS COMPLEX POLYMER IN HIGHER CONCENTRATIONS. SOURCE OF SILICON DIOXIDE. SOME HEALTH RELATED USES. THERE SEEMS TO BE NOT MANY USES FOR THIS SUBSTANCE." (This text describes the chemical reaction shown: Sodium Silicate reacts with Hydrochloric Acid to produce Sodium Chloride and Silicic Acid, which forms complex polymers and is a source of silicon dioxide with some health-related uses, though it generally has few applications). The person then adds tap water from the tall plastic bottle to the glass bowl containing the gel to dilute the mixture. They dip a yellow pH strip into the liquid, which confirms it is acidic, placing it next to a pH color chart. Next, the person uses the syringe to add more liquid from the small clear bottle to the bowl, then uses the same syringe to stir and break apart the white gel-like chunks. The video transitions to a close-up of the glass bowl, showing the white, chunky, gel-like substance with visible bubbles. The person uses a pink plastic tool to vigorously stir and break down the gel into finer pieces, with the pH strips and color chart visible in the background.

A hand with a pink spatula is actively stirring a thick, chunky, translucent white substance in a clear glass bowl, gradually adding more water to thin it out until it becomes a milky-white liquid. To the left of the bowl, a small plastic bag with a green price tag, displaying "129.50" and a barcode, is visible. Above the bag, a pH test strip and color chart are present, with the partially visible text reading "optimální pH bazénové vody" (optimal pH of pool water) and indicating pH values like "6.5", "7", and "7.5". The hand then dips a yellow pH strip into the mixture and holds it against the chart, indicating a pH level around 6. The scene then transitions to a static shot of a clear glass beaker labeled "Fisherbrand 600ml" filled with clear liquid, next to a clear plastic bottle also containing clear liquid. A small, dark-colored cat with some brown markings is visible sitting calmly behind the beaker and bottle, looking towards the viewer. All items are placed on a dark patterned surface resembling a circuit board, with a white cable visible in the background.

A person's right hand, wearing a dark wristband, holds a clear glass beaker containing a transparent liquid, positioning it over the opening of a clear plastic bottle. The bottle stands on a dark surface patterned with what resembles circuit board traces. In the background, a white power strip with several outlets is visible on a wooden shelf.

In the video segment, a person's hands are shown performing a chemical experiment on a dark-patterned surface, resembling a circuit board. Initially, a hand pours a clear liquid, identified as "sodium silicate solution," from a bottle with a white cap into a large, clear plastic bottle already containing a small amount of liquid. The bottle is then placed on the surface. Subsequently, about 500 milliliters of clear "water" are poured from a glass measuring beaker into the same plastic bottle. The person then caps the plastic bottle and shakes it vigorously, causing the clear liquids to mix and transform into a cloudy, milky-white solution. The bottle is returned to the surface. Next, the person pours a clear liquid from a white plastic bottle, labeled "RYSELINA SOLNA" (Hydrochloric acid) and "Labar," into a small, clear glass jar. Finally, the person uses a white syringe to draw liquid from the small jar and carefully injects it into the cloudy mixture in the larger plastic bottle, repeating the process multiple times. In the background, a light wooden shelf is visible with white window blinds and a white power strip connected to various black cables.

In a kitchen-like setting with a wooden shelf and horizontal blinds in the background, a person's hands are shown performing a chemical mixing experiment. To the left, a tall, clear plastic bottle is partially filled with a clear liquid. To the right, a clear glass beaker (labeled "Fisherbrand 600ml") and a small, clear glass jar are present, along with an opaque white bottle labeled "KYSELINA SOLNA" (meaning "Hydrochloric Acid") and "Label". Initially, the person uses a white syringe-like device to dispense liquid from the small glass jar into the beaker. Next, they pour a small amount of clear liquid from a separate clear glass into the plastic bottle. After this addition, the person picks up the bottle and gently swirls its contents, causing the liquid to turn uniformly cloudy and milky white. They then pour more liquid from the small clear glass into the plastic bottle. Finally, the person picks up the plastic bottle and vigorously shakes it, transforming the cloudy liquid into a thick, opaque white, seemingly solid or highly viscous substance.

A person is shown shaking a clear plastic bottle containing a cloudy white liquid and white solid chunks, attempting to mechanically process the solid. After shaking, the person inserts a red stirring rod into the bottle to stir the contents. Subsequently, a yellow pH strip is dipped into the liquid, changing color to indicate its acidity. The scene then transitions to a glass beaker with a white paper filter cone, into which the person pours the cloudy white liquid from the bottle, attempting gravitational filtration, which is visibly slow and unsuccessful. The video then cuts to an overhead shot of a black bowl containing a bluish-grey liquid. A white plastic strainer is placed over the bowl, and a person's hands are seen pushing white, gelatinous solid chunks through the strainer's mesh, breaking them into smaller particles and allowing them to fall into the liquid below. A white bottle with a label reading "KYSELINA SOLNA" (Hydrochloric Acid) is visible in the background throughout parts of the video.

The video opens with a close-up shot of a person's hand pressing a white, circular sieve containing a wet, powdery white substance over a black bowl. A clear liquid is visible below the sieve, suggesting a washing or filtering process. The substance gradually passes through the mesh. The scene then transitions to three clear plastic bottles lined up on a kitchen counter. Each bottle contains a distinct white, opaque layer at the bottom and a clear liquid layer above it. The voiceover explains that the leftmost bottle, which was not washed, appears cloudy, while the other two, which were washed three times, show a clear separation between the layers. Next, a person's hands are seen using a clear plastic tube to siphon off the clear liquid from one of the washed bottles into a kitchen sink, leaving the white settled substance at the bottom of the bottle. The person carefully adjusts the tube to drain as much clear liquid as possible without disturbing the settled solid. The video concludes with a shot of a clear glass beaker (labeled "600ml" and "Boro 3.3"), topped with a white paper filter cone secured by a red rubber band. A hand then pours the contents of a plastic bottle, presumably one of the washed samples, into the filter, indicating the final filtration step of the white solid.

In this video segment, a person initiates a filtration process by pouring a cloudy liquid from a clear plastic bottle into a white coffee filter, which is secured by a red rubber band over a glass beaker. The beaker, labeled "Fisherbrand 600ml FB33114 Boro 3.3," sits on a blue surface with a circuit board pattern. The liquid passes through the filter, leaving a clearer substance in the beaker. Later, two identical filtration setups are shown, with a person using a pink stirring tool to gently agitate the contents of the filter on the right. Finally, the person carefully lifts one of the coffee filters from a beaker over a kitchen sink and uses their hands to gently squeeze the bottom of the filter, extracting more clear liquid into the beaker below, while a white, paste-like residue remains inside the filter.

The video opens with a close-up of a person's hands squeezing a white, translucent, jelly-like substance from a plastic container into a glass beaker already containing clear liquid. The substance appears to be precipitating or being separated from a liquid. The camera then shifts to a wider shot on a blue countertop with a circuit board pattern, where the same person's hands carefully pour more of the white, lumpy substance, now contained in what looks like a piece of paper or cloth, into the glass beaker. The beaker is now mostly filled with the white, lumpy material. The scene transitions to a black wood-burning stove with visible flames inside, and a person wearing a black jacket and black pants approaches it. They place a sheet of aluminum foil on top of the stove, then carefully place the glass beaker containing the white substance onto the foil, presumably to heat it.

In this video segment, a person dressed in a black long-sleeved shirt and black pants is observed interacting with a dark gray wood-burning stove. The stove has a glass door through which vibrant orange and yellow flames are clearly visible, indicating an active fire inside. On top of the stove, a piece of aluminum foil holds a pile of white, icy or crystalline material. The person uses a small tool, resembling a scraper or spatula, to spread and flatten this white substance on the foil, seemingly to facilitate heating or drying. The camera then transitions to a close-up view of the roaring fire within the stove, highlighting the intense burning logs and bright flames. Following this, the shot returns to the top of the stove, focusing on the white material on the aluminum foil. The substance appears to be melting or transforming under the heat, becoming more translucent and solidified in some areas, suggesting a chemical process or drying.

A person, with their arm covered by a black sleeve, is seen using a flat-bladed tool with a yellow and black handle, resembling a scraper or a large flat-head screwdriver, to break apart a white, flaky, and somewhat granular substance. This white material is spread across a sheet of aluminum foil, which in turn is placed on top of a dark, metallic object that appears to be a wood-burning stove, given the orange glow visible from its lower section, suggesting a fire inside. The person repeatedly presses and scrapes the tool into the white substance, further fragmenting it and moving the pieces around on the foil.

In the video segment, a person in a dark long-sleeved garment uses a tool with a yellow and black handle, resembling a chisel or scraper, to break up a white, powdery, and somewhat crystalline substance spread on a piece of aluminum foil. The foil rests on a dark surface, possibly a stove or a heat source, as a faint orange glow is visible beneath it. The person repeatedly scrapes and chops at the substance, causing it to break into smaller particles and spread out more evenly. The scene then transitions to a clear glass beaker containing a white granular substance. A thin, dark object, possibly a wire or a wick, is embedded in the substance, and its tip is glowing red-orange, suggesting it's heated or burning. The beaker has volume markings, with "100" clearly visible near the bottom of the substance and "200" and "300" further up the side.

The video opens with a close-up of a white and orange container, possibly a small food processor or grinder, featuring a central metal shaft. Inside the container, there is a white granular substance, which the narrator identifies as dried silicon dioxide or sand, with some parts appearing as a finer powder and others as larger, chunkier pieces (around 0.8 millimeters in size). A pink plastic spatula stirs and breaks up these larger chunks of the substance. A small amount of water is poured into the container using a clear beaker in the background, to dampen the sand and reduce dust during grinding. The scene then transitions to a wider shot, showing the container now closed with an orange lid. A person's hands are visible, securing the lid and then operating the device, causing it to vibrate and emit a whirring sound, indicating the grinding process has begun. The container rests on a dark, patterned surface that resembles a circuit board.

In this video segment, a person's right hand operates an orange and white cylindrical device, seemingly grinding something, with a clear glass beaker visible in the background on a circuit board-patterned surface. After grinding, the person opens the container to reveal a light grey, fluid-like substance with a metal rod in the center. The scene then shifts to a close-up of a pile of white powdery substance on a flat white surface. A red pointed tool is used to interact with the powder, demonstrating its incredibly fine and fluid-like consistency as it flows and spreads easily with minimal friction, moving rapidly and appearing to "dance" as mentioned in the accompanying audio.

The video opens with a close-up of a glass petri dish containing a white powdery substance resting on a digital scale with a blue backlight. Initially, a hand briefly places crumpled aluminum foil into the dish before removing it. The scale's display changes rapidly from 65.59 to 66.42 as the foil is removed, and then a hand carefully lifts the petri dish slightly before setting it back down. After settling, the scale clearly displays "30.72," indicating the weight of the white powder. The scene then transitions to a white screen featuring a logo at the top that reads "ILLUSYS CHEMICAL" above an abstract geometric pattern. Below the logo, prominent text displays "SILICON DIOXIDE," followed by details about the substance: "30G ~ 81% YIELD," "BASED ON 60ML 31% HCL," "ALSO KNOWN AS QUARTZ SAND, OR SILICA," "PRECURSOR TO GLASS AND SILICON," "MAJOR COMPONENT USED IN SAND CASTING," "ADSORBENT(SILICA GEL)," and "VERY INERT MATERIAL (GLASS)." To the right of the text, a chemical structure of silicon dioxide, showing a central silicon atom double-bonded to two oxygen atoms (O=Si=O), is presented.
